ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The core device in the circuit diagram is labeled 74163, which is a 4-bit synchronous binary counter; above it are Q0, Q1, Q2, Q3 output terminals. On the right side there is a logic gate marked with “&”, whose inputs are fed back from several Q outputs, and whose output is connected to the LD/load control terminal of the 74163. In the figure, the D0, D1, D2, D3 parallel input terminals are connected together below and grounded, so the parallel loaded data is 0000. The clear/control terminals are kept in the states required for valid counting, and the clock CP input drives counting. Reasoning: The 74163 normally counts upward in binary. The feedback gate decodes a specific state from the Q outputs; according to the feedback connections in the figure and the method specified in the problem, this decoded state is binary 1101, i.e. decimal 13. When the counter reaches 13, the feedback signal acts on the LD terminal, making the next clock not continue to 14 or 15, but synchronously load D0-D3=0000. Thus the cyclic states are 0, 1, 2, ..., 13, containing 14 different states in total. Therefore this circuit forms a modulo-14 counter.

method.method_draft: Inspect the circuit image first: identify the IC as a 74163 binary counter, trace the feedback gate from the Q outputs to the load/control input, and observe that the parallel inputs D0-D3 are all grounded. Determine which binary count is decoded by the selected Q feedback lines; the feedback condition occurs at decimal 13, after which the next clock loads 0000 instead of continuing to 14 or 15. Therefore the circuit cycles through 14 distinct count states, so it is a 14-digit counter.
